clue.text: Maitresse

parts.note: surface reading: a single foreign word, perhaps a lover or a schoolteacher in France
setter's reading: the clue is itself a translation exercise, naming the French word for a woman in charge of a class or a heart

explanation.walkthrough: The one-word clue is in French; the answer says what language it is and what it means in English, and also names a teacher of that subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word maitresse translates to the English word for a lover or female teacher, and a teacher of that language bears the same title.

clue.text: Catching nothing but cold to make milk churns safe?

indicators.note: to churn is to stir violently, so the letters of the following words are beaten into a new order

parts.note: the letters of all three words, the signal word included

explanation.surface: A dairy farmer, chilled and empty-handed, wonders how to keep the milk churns secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churns' does double duty in the surface as milk containers, but its letters are part of the fodder as well as signalling the anagram; the full fodder is milk churns safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular expression for an angler's day spent getting wet and chilled while landing no fish at all.

clue.text: Result of being talked about even if one's out of it?

definitions.text: Result of being talked about even if one's out of it?

parts.note: surface reading: the consequence of being gossiped about, as when people feel their ears burning

parts.words: even if one's out of it?
parts.note: setter's reading: split the answer as two words describing burning ears, while the whole word is the range of hearing that the gossip is beyond

explanation.walkthrough: Read as EARS HOT, the answer is the folk belief that your ears burn when talked about; read whole, it is the hearing range you are out of when people discuss you.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the distance within which a sound can be heard, and split in two it describes ears said to burn when you are discussed.

clue.text: Managed to be unnatural

definitions.meaning: first meaning: succeeded in arranging something, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in seeming artificial.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of a verb for bringing something about with ingenuity, and also an adjective for laboured, artificial writing.

clue.text: Sarcastic s-setters of colours in storm and turbulence

definitions.note: two definitions run together: the sarcastic adjective plus a plural S, then fixers of dyes

indicators.note: turbulence is violent agitation, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Biting critics ply their trade amid wild weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 's-setters' is a trick: 'Sarcastic s' is the biting adjective with an S added, and 'setters of colours' is the dyer's term, both giving the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting remark is described with this adjective, and in dyeing these substances fix colours onto fabric so they do not wash out.

clue.text: Points raised satisfactorily completed

parts.note: four compass points: south, east, west, north
lifted means up

explanation.surface: Raised points of order are settled to everyone's satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically a deal or match that has been settled or secured is described as stitched closed.

clue.text: Medieval instrument of torture becomes useful

indicators.note: of here means drawn out from within the words that follow it
the words just before it are made use of as the source, yielding a run of their letters

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A medieval torture device turns out to have its uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medieval instrument of torture' sounds like the rack, but the instrument is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a pear-shaped bowed stringed instrument played in the Middle Ages, a forerunner of the fiddle.

clue.text: Do the crossword (not quickly?) and get abuse?

definitions.note: a thing that gets abused, as in sniffing glue

parts.note: what you do to a puzzle
not written in quick shorthand form, its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A slow solver gets heckled for taking so long over the crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quickly' is a pun: the word not, written quickly, is NT. Solvent abuse is the inhaling of glue or other volatile chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhaling glue fumes is known as solvent abuse, so a solvent is the thing that gets abused; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: 9, 14, 16, 18, etc the first part of 12 for writers about the district

parts.note: 12 is AGUECHEEK, whose first part, ague, is a fever, colloquially called the shakes

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the writers' word is wrapped round the district word

parts.note: pens are writing implements
a district is an area

explanation.surface: A list of cross-references sends you off to writers working round a locality.
explanation.walkthrough: Ague is a malarial fever whose shivering fits are known as the shakes. Sir Andrew, Brutus, Malvolio and Sir Toby are all characters from the Bard's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Andrew, Brutus, Malvolio and Sir Toby are characters from plays by the Bard, so they are figures belonging to his works.

clue.text: (and 12) Opening of Guardian week cheers knight (12th one, reportedly)
See 18
7 and the lady

parts.note: et is French and Latin for and
the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: Someone pairs a puzzle number with a woman, as if listing guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is the answer to 7-down, SOLVENT, used here as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile liquid dissolves fats and other substances, making it a classic example of a solvent in chemistry.

clue.text: See 9
Spur Dr Bond to drink a lot of wine

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

indicators.note: to drink is to take something inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a bond or link
a vat holds a large quantity of wine

explanation.surface: Someone tries to egg on a fictional doctor-spy to down a great deal of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr Bond' looks like a film villain or hero, but it is two separate pieces: MO is the services abbreviation for a medical officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to give them the incentive or drive to act, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Vehicle with groove in it for the honourable orator

indicators.note: with something in it says the vehicle word has another word placed inside it

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a rut is a groove worn in a road

explanation.surface: A worn-grooved bus is laid on to carry a dignified speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar, Mark Antony repeats that this conspirator 'is an honourable man', and he too addresses the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: In Julius Caesar the conspirator makes a funeral speech to the Romans and is repeatedly called honourable by Mark Antony.

clue.text: Gives good vibes to cure one's tears

indicators.note: to cure is to treat and change, so the letters after it are worked into a new form

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A positive therapy is offered as a remedy for someone's weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that strikes a chord or vibrates sympathetically gives off pleasing vibrations, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Badly translated tenth book, one notoriously abused

parts.note: mal is French for badly
vol. is short for volume
1 and 0 make the number ten, written as letters

explanation.surface: A poorly rendered tenth volume becomes infamous for its mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tenth book' gives Volume 10, VOL IO, with the digits read as letters. In Twelfth Night the steward is tricked by a forged letter and locked up as mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia's steward in Twelfth Night is cruelly gulled, mocked and imprisoned as a madman, so he is a famous victim of mistreatment.

clue.text: Modest conclusion to game

definitions.note: having no side, that is no airs
definitions.meaning: first meaning: without side, that is free of airs and pretension
second meaning: the referee's call ending a rugby match

explanation.surface: A game ends quietly without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'side' can mean conceit or putting on airs. The second sense is the rugby term for the final whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no pretension or swagger has no side, and in rugby the call at full time is the same phrase.

clue.text: (and 10) Southern Irish jug to eject knight (12th one, reportedly)
Fair that may be overtaken

definitions.meaning: second meaning: able to be passed on the road

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means just about acceptable, and literally describes something capable of being passed by another vehicle.

clue.text: Strange business with rare outcome

parts.note: biz is informal for business, as in showbiz

indicators.note: an outcome is what something works out into, so the word before it is turned into a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters of rare

explanation.surface: An odd business deal produces an unusual result.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something odd, weird or out of the ordinary, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Apple with no core, a vulgar forgery

indicators.note: having no core means the central letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: the Sturmer Pippin is an English apple variety

explanation.surface: A cored apple is passed off as a crude fake.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the seven-letter apple name is R, so dropping it leaves the answer. 'Vulgar' signals slang, not coarseness.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a stumer is a counterfeit coin, a worthless cheque or a sham, so 'vulgar' means colloquial here.

clue.text: Russian writer has an answer that''s about right to 5

indicators.note: something that goes about another surrounds it, so the answer word is wrapped around the letter for right

parts.note: from the dismissive phrase 'the answer's a lemon', an unsatisfactory reply
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A Russian author offers a reply that is nearly correct to question five.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5-down but is just the Roman numeral. Mikhail Lermontov wrote A Hero of Our Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Lermontov was a nineteenth-century Russian Romantic poet and novelist, author of A Hero of Our Time.

clue.text: Start where the filming is done

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the beginning of something
second meaning: read as two words, on the film set

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a beginning or commencement, and split into two words it locates actors in the studio during a shoot.

clue.text: Be removed from Ms Bhutto (official)

indicators.note: removed from says the first word is taken away out of the name that follows

parts.note: Benazir Bhutto, twice prime minister of Pakistan
taken as written

explanation.surface: A call for Pakistan's former leader to be ousted from office.
explanation.walkthrough: '(official)' looks like a parenthetical comment on the surface, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British India a nazir was a native court official or a minor government functionary, a historical title.

clue.text: Sort of dressing makes one annoyed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word that precedes dressing for wearing the other sex's clothes

explanation.surface: Some salad dressing puts a diner in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests salad, but the first sense is cross-dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing clothes of the opposite sex is cross-dressing, and the same word as an adjective means irritated or angry.

clue.text: Arms, etc I set on fire when embraced by 18 10's wife

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the preceding words sit within the wife's name

parts.note: Sir Toby Belch marries Olivia's gentlewoman Maria at the end of Twelfth Night
taken as written
lit means ignited

explanation.surface: An arsonist torches weapons in the arms of a knight's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: ILIT goes inside MARIA, after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectors use this term for military memorabilia such as weapons, uniforms and medals, hence arms and the like.

clue.text: Setter's model in grave to head into obscurity

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the next word, splitting it

parts.note: grave means solemn
the Model T Ford
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: The compiler's mannequin is buried, its head vanishing into darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SERIOUS after its S, giving STERIOUS; a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means the quality of being puzzling and hard to understand, a synonym for obscurity.
